Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 61, English)
Kalyan Lok, the Dimension Principle, and Jaap-for -Others: A Live Satsang on Rebirth, Pitru Protection, and the Kul Devta Revelation

Sour ce: A live, highly interactive Sunday satsang session with extensive sangat participation (named participants include Shivraam Bhaiya, Anshu, Gupta ji, Upendra Kumar , and Srinivas ji). This document is Part I of III — Knowledge Base, Q&A Pairs, and Curated Conversational Q&A.

1. Opening shaktipaat prayer . The session opens with a prayer sadhaks may of fer at the start of any sitting: "He Hanuman ji Maharaj, Parikshit Bhaiya ko sakshi maankar aapke shri charno mein Jai Siyaram ka jaap samarpit karta hoon/karti hoon. Kripa karke ise sweekar keejiye. He Prabhu mujhe bhi apni sharan mein leejiye." Offering this jaap in this way , with Parikshit Bhaiya as witness, is described as bringing the practitioner directly under divine grace.

2. Three foundational questions framed for this session. Bhaiya opens by naming three questions to address: how relationships form across rebirths and whether the cycle of rebirth can be stopped; what happens inside Kalyan Lok and what Kalyan Lok actually is; and what "aura" is, what shakti is, what a ghost/pitru is, and what drishti (subtle sight) actually is.

3. Sour ce of all teaching. Bhaiya repeats a recurring disclaimer: everything taught comes solely from what his own Gurudev (Hanuman Ji Maharaj) reveals to him — he has not read it in any book nor learned it from any other person. He notes, however , that the Upanishads themselves are extremely powerful texts, and that when viewed through the "third eye," dif ferent layers and Dimensions open within them that have not yet been explored publicly .

4. Upcoming Upanishad course. An upcoming course (tar geted for completion by the end of February) will cover 9 of the 1 1 major Upanishads, from Ishavasya Upanishad through Mandukya, Prashna, and others, including how the subtle (astral) world connects to and moves between the physical world.

5. Why negativity needs somewher e to go. Any negativity or pitru removed from a person's body during a havan cannot simply be released into open space — it does not "sit" anywhere on its own. This is illustrated by the historical pattern of village bhoot-pret removers ("jhaad-phook"): even when such a person has real shakti, their own household eventually deteriorates (family conflict, financial decline, physical ailments) after a few years of this work, specifically among those who have shakti but lack drishti (subtle sight).

6. The four elements of a person's spiritual capacity . Every person has: a Dimension (a level determining which entities/negativities are visible to and controllable by them); mantra shakti ; grahan shakti (capacity to receive/absorb); and prayog shakti (capacity to apply/use). Together , these determine what a person can remove.

7. The cor e Dimension rule for removing negativity . A person can only remove a negativity whose own Dimension is lower than their own. If a negativity's Dimension is equal to or higher than the checker's, it simply will not be visible to that checker at all — not because it isn't there, but because it is beyond that checker's Dimension to perceive.

8. Why differ ent practitioners give differ ent "aura check" r esults for the same person. This explains why a sadhak may be told at one place that they have a specific negativity/pitru issue, and told elsewhere ("at some other dham/temple") that "nothing is wrong" with them — the second checker's Dimension may simply be lower than the negativity's Dimension, so it remains invisible to them, even though the same symptoms persist.

9. Why Bhaiya personally checks aura monthly rather than delegating. Despite having many trained mentors, Bhaiya checks aura himself because subtle negativity frequently crosses an individual checker's Dimension and appears instead as ordinary "maya" (illusion) rather than as visible negativity . He states his Gurudev's own sight ("nazar") has never missed anyone, however many hundreds are checked (400–600+ referenced in this session).

10. The Shivraam Bhaiya case — a live illustration of the Dimension principle. Shivraam Bhaiya, present for about a week at this session, is described as having an extraordinarily powerful aura and drishti that opened at least a year and a half earlier , practicing at the "fourth stage" of jaap. A month prior , he visited another powerful practitioner (a devotee of the Divine Mother/"Mata ki bhakt") who touched his head/third eye "to see him." Despite Shivraam Bhaiya's own great devotion, other checkers at Ashaeiynn initially found nothing on him — until Bhaiya's own Gurudev directly indicated, through him, that a yogini shakti (a subtle female spirit-power associated with highly advanced sadhaks, which never travels alone but with two attendant "sevikas") had attached itself to him during that visit, invisible to lesser checkers precisely because his own advancing Dimension had crossed theirs.

1 1. Why r egular mantra-jaap makes a person cr oss Dimensions — and why this itself cr eates risk. Regular mantra jaap steadily raises a practitioner's own Dimension. A consequence often overlooked is that this same rise means the person can now attract or be visited by higher -Dimension entities, which lower -level checkers (or the person themself, without drishti) genuinely cannot perceive — this is precisely why continuing, structured, guided practice remains necessary even for advanced practitioners.

12. "Chhote log bhakti se chukte nahi" (small people never skip devotion) — the pride warning. Bhaiya cautions that practitioners new to bhakti follow every instruction obediently , but as soon as they receive drishti or shakti, ego and "maya" often creep in — leading some to start finding fault with the teacher (criticizing dress, mannerisms, or small details) and to feel they no longer need guidance, precisely because they mistakenly believe their own sight now equals or exceeds their guru's.

13. As Dimension rises, challenges rise pr oportionately . Small disturbances stop bothering an advanced practitioner altogether — but larger , more significant challenges ("pareeksha," tests) begin to appear at each higher Dimension. This is framed as an unavoidable and continuous feature of spiritual advancement, not a sign of failure.

14. What Kalyan Lok is. Kalyan Lok is a bridge r ealm created by Bhaiya's Gurudev (with permission obtained from 1 1 devi-devatas) between Ashaeiynn and Pretraj Sarkar . It exists to serve two purposes: to process/cleanse negativity of any kind, and to process/cleanse pitru (ancestral spirits) of any kind.

15. Kalyan Lok's internal structur e. Kalyan Lok contains 16 distinct sections ("loks"/categories); negativities and pitrus are sorted into sections by category . Its function is described as intensive purification — cleansing negativity or pitru until it becomes "shuddh" (pure).

16. The cleansing/"corr ection" mechanism. Purification within Kalyan Lok is compared to beating dust out of a mattress — described plainly as corrective discipline ("jiski jaisi chamdi, uski waisi dhamdi" — the thickness of correction matches the thickness of one's accumulated impurity). This is explicitly framed not as arbitrary cruelty but as necessary removal of deeply layered impurity ("malinta").

17. The vow taken befor e release. Once a negativity/pitru is purified, a vow is extracted from it: a commitment to future devotion (bhakti) and surrender to the guru. After this vow , it is sent onward to Pretraj Sarkar , where it waits, doing jaap, until its yoni (lifeform/rebirth state) changes.

18. Where Kalyan Lok's energy comes fr om. Kalyan Lok is powered entirely by the combined shakti of the 1 1 devi-devatas who granted permission for its creation; the operational "cost" and responsibility of running it rests on Bhaiya's Gurudev . Every realm/lok is
described as having its own ener gy channel and internal working system, requiring someone dedicated to maintaining it continuously .

19. The two-hour daily jaap thr eshold for sending negativity to Kalyan Lok. Anyone who does at least two hours of daily "Jai Siyaram" jaap regularly has the capacity to send negativity they encounter to Kalyan Lok themselves. Bhaiya is explicit that this capacity comes entirely from his Gurudev's own vachan (word/promise), not from Bhaiya himself.

20. The one-way rule — and its r eal-world exception. Once something is sent to Kalyan Lok by its own will and structure, it can never return on its own — this is stated as an absolute guarantee for anyone's own pitru sent there by their own choice. However , a dif ferent mechanism exists: any subtle power (including a pitru sent to Kalyan Lok) can be recalled by someone else through an invocation/of fering ("bhog"), because all shakti has an inherent "pulling stamina" that responds to invocation (aahan shakti) — the same mechanism by which a devotee calls their guru to mind.

21. Why pitru-r elated prayers specifically ask entities to "stay outside the aura and outside the home." Based on aura-checking data from roughly 2,000–3,000+ cases, it has been repeatedly observed that even after a pitru is sent to Kalyan Lok, family members or those performing tantrik rituals can call that same pitru back via "bhog" (ritual of fering), causing renewed problems — hence the specific protective prayer wording.

22. The protective prayer appr oach r ecommended by Bhaiya's Gurudev . Rather than trying to fight or remove a pitru directly (which is described as not something one "can do" to a pitru), the recommended remedy is to pray specifically and by name for all family members that no pitru be allowed into one's "aura mandal" (aura field) or home, and to ask Hanuman Ji Maharaj for a protective "lock" — this creates a shield such that even a pitru summoned back via bhog cannot cross in; it may linger nearby but cannot cause harm.

23. Lifetime commitment to this prayer is described as essential. Bhaiya states that households where pitrus have historically caused trouble should never stop this specific prayer — doing so consistently is described as creating a protective shield strong enough to prevent pitru interference even for future generations.

24. What to do when a new death occurs in the family . If a household regularly does this pitru-distancing prayer and someone in the family passes away , that newly-deceased person should be specifically named in the prayer ("please also keep [name], who has just passed, outside") and explicitly granted "pitru" status in the prayer — otherwise a newly-formed pitru may linger inside the home itself while other pitrus remain kept outside.

25. Which pitrus become "pr et" (restless/troublesome) vs. which ascend. A pitru who is "worthy" (lāyak) is taken upward by deva shakti before ever becoming a lingering household presence. Pitrus who linger and trouble a household are, by contrast, those who were "unworthy" (nalāyak) in this sense — Bhaiya notes with some regret how often family members themselves (rather than outsiders) are the source of a household's suf fering in this era.

26. The "new market upgrade" — a tantrik technique to specifically warn against. A newer , more dangerous tantrik technique directly of fers "bhog" to a person's own household pitru and then deliberately binds a fresh negativity to that same pitru before releasing both together onto the tar get. Because it tar gets one's own pitru, ordinary household deva-worship and puja cannot counter it — deities protect against external negativity but will not act against a person's own pitru. The only defense described is the same distancing prayer (asking the pitru to stay away), not confrontation.

27. Practical r emedy for anyone facing sudden difficulty . As an accessible starting point, lighting 1 1 diyas daily for just three days , with sincere prayer , is described as producing rapid, tangible benefit — corroborated, per Bhaiya, by over 100 people reporting this result in the preceding month alone.

28. On lamp oil and offerings — material does carry some impact, but no single material is mandated. Whatever material is used (mustard oil, ghee, sesame oil, or even a candle) is accepted according to one's bhaav (devotional intent) — Bhaiya's Gurudev has never specified one exact required material. What matters most is regularity and sincerity of the of fering, not the specific substance.

29. The "science" aside on lamp materials. In response to a technical/scientific follow-up question, Bhaiya notes descriptively that dif ferent substances (e.g., ghee vs. plain oil) carry dif ferent ener gy content and dif ferent ignition temperatures, and that duration of a diya's burning also af fects its impact — without prescribing one substance as spiritually superior to another .

30. Drishti (subtle sight): the "instrument vs. pr ojector light" framework. A person's drishti is like an instrument (a screen/device) granted by the devi-devatas; but what is pr ojected onto it — i.e., what is actually shown — depends entirely on which subtle entity is "standing with" that person at the time. The instrument is universal; the content shown is determined by the shakti behind it.

31. Drishti has 77,000 layers; only "divine drishti" is opened by devtas specifically . Not all opened drishti is the same — some show ghosts/negativity directly (e.g., "karna-pishachini" siddhi shows negativity directly and in full detail), while divine drishti granted through Ashaeiynn requires the practitioner to actively ask ("Baba, please show me the negativity") before anything negative becomes visible at all — it will not appear uninvited.
32. Drishti-opening statistics. Over roughly the past two years, on average one person's drishti has opened per week through this practice; this rate has reportedly now doubled.

33. The screen given after drishti opens. After drishti opens, practitioners are eventually given "a screen" (an Ashaeiynn-specific viewing capacity) that allows them to fully dif ferentiate what they are perceiving.

34. Jaap vs. meditation — why the energy differs despite both using mantra. Framed through the milk analogy: the same milk produces curd, paneer , and ghee — one base element, three distinct products, depending on process. Jaap (mantra recitation) and meditation (dhyan) likewise dif fer in resulting ener gy despite sharing the same mantra, based on the distinct "process" applied.

35. What "dut" (messengers) ar e. Dut are subtle bodies who have progressed beyond Kalyan Lok and now serve directly at Baba's (Hanuman Ji's) feet — ef fectively Baba's own "army ," drawn from among advanced subtle bodies who have earned this position through service.

36. How to become a "dut" of Baba. No formal qualification is required to become a dut — only love and surrender toward Baba. Bhaiya states plainly that Baba himself creates the necessary qualification in a devotee who has sincere love and submission.

37. The Om (अ -उ -म ) teaching, r eferencing the Prashna Upanishad. Referencing the story of six sages (from Pipplad Rishi's teaching in the Prashna Upanishad) who sought knowledge and were told to first spend a year practicing tapasya and brahmacharya to prove their worthiness, Bhaiya explains that the three sounds अ (a) , उ (u), and म (m) each historically had their own distinct sadhana and distinct results. When combined, they together confer attainment of the formless Brahm (nirakar Brahm) — this combined utterance is what is called "Om."

38. The Mandukya Upanishad and the turiya state. The Mandukya Upanishad specifically describes the turiya state — a deep meditative condition in which a person remains in a fully awakened state even while in deep meditative absorption, described as an element of "sakshaat samadhi." This Upanishad also details the individual significance of Om and the separate sadhanas of अ, उ , and म .

39. Rebirth and the "best of thr ee/two options" framework. Before rebirth, a soul is generally presented with the "best of three" (or at minimum "best of two") available options for its next incarnation, and it chooses the best among those available — meaning that if all available options are poor , the outcome will reflect that limitation.

40. The moksha r eaffirmation callback. Reasserting a teaching from a prior session: "moksha jaisa kuch nahi hota" (there is no such thing as literal liberation/moksha in the traditional sense). When a past case of someone in Ghaziabad (near Meerut) who attained "jeete ji moksha" (liberation while still alive) is raised, Bhaiya clarifies: "jeete ji moksha" specifically means that the person's karmic backlog was clear ed ("karmo ko kaat liya... zero") — it is a fresh start from zero, not an end to the ongoing creation of karma altogether , since karma will continue to be generated as long as one lives and acts.

41. Helping elderly family members thr ough jaap — what is and isn't possible. For someone who has already passed away , nothing further can be done. For a living elder who listens to and trusts a practitioner , real "uddhar" (upliftment) is possible if that elder is
guided to take up their own regular , disciplined mantra jaap with sankalp (resolve/intention) — at which point spiritual work replaces bodily-symptom-focused ef fort.

42. Why jaap cannot simply be "dedicated" to someone who does no jaap themselves — the ghee/digestion analogy . Illustrated through "Gupta ji": if Gupta ji is physically weak, one could try to directly feed him ener gy-rich foods (almonds, cashews, raisins, ghee) — but if Gupta ji does not move, exercise, or exert himself, his body cannot digest and convert that input into usable strength. Similarly , dedicating jaap-shakti to someone who does no jaap of their own does not work, because their capacity to "digest" and use that shakti simply does not exist — the shakti transferred can, at most, amplify an existing ef fort, not create one from nothing.

43. The Saturday collective jaap only "attaches" to those alr eady doing their own jaap. Bhaiya states plainly that he does not personally do jaap on behalf of people who have never done any jaap themselves, regardless of how much money is of fered (explicitly rejecting sums up to ₹1 lakh of fered by visitors for this purpose) — jaap-shakti of fered on someone's behalf only works for people already practicing their own jaap, where it functions as an amplifier (e.g., someone doing one hour personally might have it ef fectively amplified to ten).

44. Unused, undigested devotional energy dir ected at a non-practicing person can itself become a negativity risk. When rituals/puja are done on behalf of ancestors who never did their own jaap (e.g., near death), the of fered ener gy is "not digested" and remains unused ("dhara ka dhara reh jaata hai") — and because unused excess ener gy does not simply disappear , it risks being drawn upon or misused by another negativity .

45. Practical guidance for jaap-on-behalf-of-others. The correct approach is proportional and collaborative: e.g., "you do 5 minutes, I will do 15"; "you do 10 minutes, I will do an hour" — but the person themselves must still participate to some degree; jaap purely and entirely done "for" someone who does nothing themselves does not transfer benefit to them.

46. Mahamrityunjaya jaap performed by pandits — a genuineness test. Bhaiya frames the value of a pandit performing Mahamrityunjaya jaap on someone's behalf through a direct, practical test: if the person for whom it's done actually feels a tangible dif ference, the jaap is genuine and working for them; if no dif ference is felt, the resulting ener gy from that jaap is likely benefiting someone else (potentially the pandit or another party), not the intended recipient. The Mahamrityunjaya mantra itself is af firmed as genuinely and literally conferring a form of immortality/protection when done with real sankalp and discipline (niyam-kanoon, "raksha-suraksha ke saath").

47. Drishti layer capacity for an average person vs. with guru's help. An average person can, across a lifetime, cross approximately 60,000 layers of drishti on their own; with a guru's help, a person can access essentially any "screen" without this ordinary limitation.

48. Spiritual awakening vs. enlightenment, distinguished. Spiritual awakening means realizing that "there is something in spirituality" and being drawn toward exploring it further . Enlightenment ("bodh") is a far deeper state — comparable to what Lord Buddha attained — in which every question finds its answer .

49. Declining to discuss the Kalki avatar . When asked directly about the Kalki avatar (an avatar associated with the end of the current age/kaliyug), Bhaiya explicitly declines to speculate, stating he only teaches what his Gurudev has personally shown or told him, and Kalki avatar has not been part of that direct revelation.

50. Kul devta ("family deity") vs. pitru worship timing. During periods normally reserved for remembering pitrus (ancestors) in ritual worship, Bhaiya recommends instead remembering one's kul devta (family/clan deity) at that time, since this properly channels the grace one seeks.

51. "Pitruk ke pitru" — ancestors above the level of devtas. A special category of pitru exists above the devta lok itself, called pitru lok — considered a lok higher than the deva lok. Ordinary practitioners lack the capacity/"aukat" to summon such a high-level pitru down directly; this can only happen through the sanction of one's kul devta, and even then, all credit and worship goes to the kul devta, not the summoned high pitru.

52. Bageshwar Sarkar and Pandokar Sarkar as examples of "jeete ji amar" (immortal while living) lineage-heads. In lar ge, established spiritual lineages/dhams (referencing Bageshwar Dham and Pandokar Sarkar as examples), the shakti standing behind the current lineage head's ancestors ("dada guru") is described as continuously and permanently present ("jeete ji amar") across generations of successors — this state is attained through total, exclusive devotion ("ananya bhakti"), such that the shakti remains connected to the body/lineage seat even without being permanently housed in one physical body , appearing as needed.

53. Pitru vs. purvaj — terminology clarification. To reduce confusion, Bhaiya distinguishes: "purvaj" broadly refers to anyone who has passed away and is related by blood/family , while "pitru" is used more specifically — though the two terms are lar gely treated as synonyms in casual use ("pitru" for those inside a family's own lineage vs. entities more generally outside it, sometimes loosely called "pret" by contrast).

54. Blood-r elation dosh does not automatically transfer beyond dir ect blood r elations. A dosh (af fliction) present in an in-law's bloodline (e.g., a sibling's spouse's family) does not directly transfer onto the practitioner's own family , though some indirect/partial effect on the directly-married-in individual is acknowledged as possible.

55. Karma is "r eplaced," not simply erased. Karma cannot be permanently "cut" or eliminated — rather , existing karma can be replaced with dif ferent karma through spiritual work; the underlying principle that action (karma) continues as an ongoing feature of living remains constant.

56. Privacy as a strict, guru-mandated policy . From the very first day of Ashaeiynn's public YouT ube presence, Bhaiya instructed his technical team never to publish anything that would breach the privacy of the community or its practices, on the principle that these teachings and techniques are reserved specifically for those whom the guru himself chooses to bring — never advertised or revealed to outsiders.

57. WhatsApp community migration. Members using the WhatsApp community are being automatically migrated to Ashaeiynn's of ficial community platform, including a separate community for havan-related coordination; this transition will happen automatically with prior notice.

58. The kul devta r evelation — a described turning point. For roughly six months, many practitioners had asked Bhaiya to reveal their specific kul devta (family deity) by name, given how much emphasis is placed on kul devta reverence — but historically , Bhaiya's Gurudev revealed this for only about 2 out of every 10 people who asked, leaving the majority without an answer . After continued prayerful requests, Bhaiya's Gurudev eventually granted a specific sadhana enabling far more complete and direct revelation — Bhaiya describes now regularly and directly speaking aloud kul devta and kul devi names (often names entirely unrecorded anywhere online or in any published source) to individual practitioners, describing this moment, each time it happens, as deeply moving — sometimes bringing him to tears — precisely because these are names with no external verifiability that nonetheless resonate immediately and specifically for the person receiving them.

59. This kul devta r evelation is deliberately kept low-pr ofile. Despite its significance, Bhaiya states this specific capability/sadhana is intentionally not publicized, on the principle (again) that this service is meant only for those already under the guru's grace, not for public promotion.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

A practitioner can only perceive/remove a negativity whose Dimension is lower than their own — higher -Dimension entities are invisible to lower -Dimension checkers, which is why aura-check results can genuinely dif fer between locations. Kalyan Lok is a bridge realm (16 sections) between Ashaeiynn and Pretraj Sarkar , created with the permission of 1 1 devidevatas, used to cleanse both negativity and pitru through a corrective ("beating"/discipline) process before a vow of future devotion is extracted and the entity is sent onward.

Anyone doing at least 2 hours of daily "Jai Siyaram" jaap has the capacity to send negativity encountered to Kalyan Lok themselves. Once sent to Kalyan Lok by its own choice, an entity never returns on its own — but it can be recalled by someone else (family member or tantrik) via a "bhog" (ritual of fering), which is why specific protective prayers naming family members and asking pitrus to stay outside the aura/home are essential and should never be dropped. A newer , more dangerous tantrik technique binds a fresh negativity directly onto a person's own household pitru before releasing both onto a tar get — household deities cannot act against a person's own pitru, so the only defense is the distancing prayer , not direct confrontation. 1 1 daily diyas for 3 days, with sincere prayer , is of fered as an accessible, fast-acting remedy for general dif ficulty; lamp material (oil, ghee, or candle) is accepted according to bhaav (devotional intent) — no single substance is spiritually mandated. Drishti works like an instrument with a "projector light" — the device is universal, but what it shows depends entirely on which subtle power stands with the practitioner; divine drishti (through Ashaeiynn) will not show negativity unless the practitioner explicitly asks to see it. Jaap-shakti done "on behalf of" someone only benefits that person if they are already doing their own jaap — it can amplify existing ef fort but cannot create benefit from nothing (the ghee/digestion analogy); the Saturday collective jaap therefore only attaches to those already practicing. "Moksha jaisa kuch nahi hota" — the recurring teaching that literal liberation isn't the correct frame; "jeete ji moksha" specifically means an individual's karmic backlog is cleared to zero, not that karma-generation itself ends. Karma is replaced, not permanently erased. Kul devta (family deity) should be remembered specifically during periods traditionally reserved for pitru worship; "pitruk ke pitru" refers to a rare higher class of ancestor above deva lok, accessible only through a kul devta's sanction. This session included genuine live sangat interaction (named participants, a live yogini-shakti case, personal questions, and a moving closing testimony), so Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) is included for this session. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 61, English)
Kalyan Lok, the Dimension Principle, and Jaap-for -Others
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live satsang session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siyaram."

Q1. What is Kalyan Lok? A: Per this teaching, Kalyan Lok is a bridge realm created by Bhaiya's Gurudev (with permission from 1 1 devi-devatas) between Ashaeiynn and Pretraj Sarkar , used to cleanse both negativity and pitru of any kind before they move onward.

Q2. How many sections does Kalyan Lok have, and how ar e entities sorted into them? A: Per this teaching, Kalyan Lok has 16 distinct sections, and negativities/pitrus are sorted into them by category (e.g., whether they are a pitru or a pret).

Q3. What actually happens to a negativity or pitru once it's sent to Kalyan Lok? A: Per this teaching, it under goes an intensive purification/correction process (compared to beating dust out of a mattress) proportional to how much impurity it carries, after which a vow of future devotion and surrender is extracted before it is sent onward to Pretraj Sarkar to await a change in its life-form.

Q4. Can a pitru or negativity ever return once sent to Kalyan Lok? A: Per this teaching, it will never return on its own accord — that is guaranteed. However , it can be recalled by someone else (a family member or a tantrik practitioner) through an invocation/ritual of fering ("bhog"), since all shakti carries an inherent "pulling" responsiveness to invocation.

Q5. Why do pitru-r elated prayers specifically ask entities to stay "outside the aura and outside the home"? A: Per this teaching, because aura-checking data (from roughly 2,000–3,000+ cases) has repeatedly shown that pitrus sent to Kalyan Lok are sometimes called back by family members or tantrik rituals via ritual of ferings, so a specific ongoing protective prayer is needed rather than a onetime removal.

Q6. What is the r ecommended r emedy against a pitru that keeps tr oubling a household? A: Per this teaching, rather than trying to fight or remove the pitru directly , one should pray specifically and consistently , naming all family members, asking that no pitru enter the household's aura field, and asking for Hanuman Ji Maharaj's protective "lock" — this creates a shield that prevents harm even if the pitru lingers nearby .

Q7. What should be added to this pr otective prayer if a new death occurs in the family? A: Per this teaching, the newly deceased person should be specifically named in the prayer , asked to also remain outside the home/aura, and explicitly granted "pitru" status — otherwise this newly-formed pitru may linger and roam inside the home itself even while other pitrus are kept outside.

Q8. Why do some pitrus become r estless/troublesome ("pr et") while others don't linger at all? A: Per this teaching, a "worthy" pitru is taken upward by deva shakti before it can ever become a lingering household presence; those who remain and cause trouble are, per this teaching, generally the "unworthy" ones.

Q9. What is the "new market upgrade" tantrik technique Bhaiya warns about? A: Per this teaching, it is a newer , more dangerous technique where a tantrik directly of fers ritual "bhog" to a person's own household pitru and binds a fresh negativity to it before releasing both onto the tar get — since it uses the tar get's own pitru, ordinary household deity worship cannot counter it (deities protect against outside negativity but will not act against one's own pitru), so the only defense described is the distancing prayer .

Q10. Why can a practitioner sometimes not per ceive a negativity that another practitioner clearly sees? A: Per this teaching, every entity — including negativity — has its own Dimension, and a person can only perceive/remove a negativity whose Dimension is lower than their own; if it's equal or higher , it becomes invisible to that checker , appearing at most as ordinary "maya."

Q1 1. Who is Shivraam Bhaiya, and what happened in his case, per this teaching? Q14. What warning does Bhaiya give about pride after receiving drishti or shakti? Q15. Do challenges disappear as a person's Dimension rises? A: No — per this teaching, small, petty disturbances stop bothering an advanced practitioner entirely , but proportionally lar ger tests/challenges appear at each higher Dimension; this is described as a continuous, unavoidable feature of advancement, not evidence of failure.

Q16. What is the minimum daily jaap needed to gain the capacity to send negativity to Kalyan Lok oneself? A: Per this teaching, at least two hours of daily "Jai Siyaram" jaap, done regularly , grants this capacity — attributed entirely to Bhaiya's Gurudev's own vachan (promise), not to Bhaiya personally .

Q17. Is ther e one specific oil or material r equired for a diya? Q18. Does the material used in a diya carry any measurable differ ence in effect? Q19. What is the quick r emedy Bhaiya r ecommends for someone facing sudden difficulty? Q20. How does drishti (subtle sight) actually work, per this teaching's "instrument vs. pr ojector light" framework? A: Per this teaching, drishti is like an instrument/screen granted by the devi-devatas, but what is actually shown on it depends entirely on which subtle entity is "projecting" onto it at that moment — i.e., who is standing with the practitioner determines what they see, not the instrument itself.

Q21. Does opened drishti automatically show ghosts and negativity? A: No — per this teaching, divine drishti (as granted through Ashaeiynn) will not show negativity unless the practitioner explicitly asks to see it ("Baba, please show me the negativity"); other
forms of drishti (e.g., karna-pishachini siddhi) do show negativity directly and unprompted, but that is a dif ferent kind of sight altogether .

Q22. Roughly how many layers does drishti have, and how many can an average person cr oss in a lifetime? A: Per this teaching, drishti has approximately 77,000 layers overall; an average person can cross approximately 60,000 of these across a lifetime on their own, while with a guru's help a person can access essentially any "screen" without this ordinary limit.

Q23. How often does a practitioner's drishti typically open thr ough this practice? A: Per this teaching, over roughly the past two years, on average one person's drishti has opened per week, and this rate has reportedly now doubled.

Q24. Why do jaap and meditation pr oduce differ ent results even though both use the same mantra? Q25. What ar e "dut" (messengers), per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, dut are subtle bodies who have progressed beyond Kalyan Lok and now serve directly at Baba's (Hanuman Ji's) feet, functioning ef fectively as Baba's own army , drawn from advanced subtle bodies who earned this position through service.

Q26. How does one become a "dut" of Baba? A: Per this teaching, no formal qualification is required — only love and surrender toward Baba; Baba himself creates the necessary qualification in a devotee with sincere devotion.

Q27. What is the Om ( अ -उ -म ) teaching r eferenced from the Prashna Upanishad? A: Per this teaching, referencing the story of six sages who approached Pipplad Rishi and were told to first complete a year of tapasya and brahmacharya to prove worthiness, the three sounds अ (a), उ (u), and म (m) each had distinct historical sadhanas and distinct results; combined, they confer the formless Brahm (nirakar Brahm), and this combined utterance is what is called "Om."

Q28. What does the Mandukya Upanishad add to this teaching about Om? A: Per this teaching, the Mandukya Upanishad specifically describes the "turiya" state — a deep meditative condition in which a person remains fully awake even in deep meditative absorption, an element of "sakshaat samadhi" — and elaborates further on Om's significance and the separate sadhanas of अ, उ , and म .

Q29. Does a soul get to fr eely choose any incarnation befor e rebirth? A: Per this teaching, a soul is generally of fered the "best of three" (or at minimum "best of two") available options before rebirth and chooses the best among those — meaning if all available options are poor , the resulting incarnation reflects that limitation.

Q30. Does moksha (liberation) r eally exist, per this teaching? A: No — per this teaching, this is a reaf firmed prior teaching: "moksha jaisa kuch nahi hota" (there is no such thing as literal moksha in the traditional sense).

Q31. Then what does "jeete ji moksha" (liberation while still alive) actually mean, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, it specifically means the person's karmic backlog has been cleared to zero — a fresh start — not that karma-generation itself has ended, since karma continues to be created as long as a person lives and acts.

Q32. Can jaap be done on behalf of an elderly family member who does none themselves? Q33. What is the r ecommended appr oach for helping a family member spiritually who is only willing to do a little jaap themselves? A: Per this teaching, a proportional, collaborative approach is recommended — e.g., "you do 5 minutes, I will do 15," or "you do 10 minutes, I will do an hour" — since some active participation from the person themselves is required for any benefit to actually transfer .

Q34. Does Bhaiya perform jaap on behalf of anyone who asks and pays, even if they've never done jaap themselves? Q35. Is it risky to perform rituals/puja on behalf of someone (e.g., a dying r elative) who never did their own jaap? Q36. Does Mahamrityunjaya jaap performed by a pandit on someone's behalf actually work? The mantra itself is af firmed as genuinely and literally capable of conferring protection/immortality-like benefit when done with real sankalp and discipline.

Q37. What is the differ ence between spiritual awakening and enlightenment, per this teaching? Q38. Did Bhaiya explain anything about the Kalki avatar in this session? A: No — per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly declined to discuss the Kalki avatar , stating he only teaches what his Gurudev has personally shown or revealed to him, and this has not been part of that direct revelation.

Q42. What is the differ ence between "pitru" and "purvaj," per this teaching?
